title: Why Do Cows Spend 8 Hours a Day Chewing Burps? 🐄
description:
Why do cows burp up their lunch and chew it again? A cow's one stomach has four compartments, and microbes in the giant rumen ferment tough grass that cows can't digest alone.

topic: Why do cows have a stomach with four compartments?
script: Cows burp up their lunch on purpose, and you'd never guess why. Grass is really hard to digest. Its walls are made of cellulose, and cows can't break that down alone. So one stomach has four rooms. Room one is the rumen, a vat holding up to forty gallons. It's packed with tiny microbes, and they ferment the grass. Room two, the honeycomb, sorts the pieces. Big chunks go back up her throat, as a soggy ball called cud. She chews it again, for about eight hours a day. Fine mush slides into room three, where water gets squeezed out. Room four is the true stomach, full of acid, like yours. All that fermenting makes gas, hundreds of litres of methane a day, and she burps it out. So, would you chew your lunch twice?
key_facts: One stomach with four compartments: rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum (MSU)
Rumen holds up to 40 gallons in a mature cow (MSU; other sources differ, hence 'up to')
Rumen microbes digest cellulose (MSU, Science Learning Hub)
Reticulum sorts small particles onward, larger stay for further digestion (MSU, Science Learning Hub)
Cows ruminate about a third of the day, ~8 hours (MSU; Purdue 35-40%)
Omasum absorbs water; abomasum is the true stomach with acid (all sources)
Cows burp 250-500 litres of methane a day (Science Learning Hub)
